turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Arjun, come sit, I will do the peak flow before doctor calls you. Blow out as hard as you can, one long blast.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): This blowing is unnecessary only. I am perfectly fine, my mother dragged me. The serial on the waiting-room TV was just getting good, I missed the ending.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): That blow was half-hearted. Best was two seventy... no, sorry, I was reading the wrong column. Best of three is three hundred litres per minute.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): You said three twenty, I heard three twenty. Don't write it down wrong and make a case out of nothing.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): No, it is three hundred, and three hundred is what I am entering. Oxygen saturation is ninety-six percent, pulse is ninety-eight.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ninety-six is normal, no? So there is nothing wrong with me. We can go home.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor will see you. Your mother told me outside you get breathless on one flight of stairs, and you did not sleep at all last night from the wheeze.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Amma panics, she is like that only. I slept fine. On the stairs there was a little huff, nothing more.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Um, one second, this screen has frozen again. Arjun, yes? Sorry, what brings you today?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Just a small wheeze after a cold. It is nothing, doctor. I would not have come, amma forced me.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Wheeze, right. Since when? Say it again, I was clicking the wrong tab.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): The wheeze is small only. It started Thursday... no, no, Wednesday night, so five days. The cold was before that, and the cold is finished.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Five days. Is there a cough with it, or only the wheeze?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): A little dry cough. Hardly anything. I am not bothered by it, honestly.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever? Any chest pain when you breathe?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. No chest pain. I told you, it is mild only.
[SEG0017] person_1 (NURSE): He is brushing it off, doctor. Mother said he was sitting up in the night with a whistle from the chest.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I was not sitting up all night. I slept. I woke one time, that is all, everyone does that.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): One minute, the medication list will not open. Which inhalers are you actually using?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Two pumps, a blue one and a brown one. I get them mixed up, I won't lie.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tell me how you take each one. Slowly, this cursor is jumping.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): When the chest gets tight I take the brown one, because brown looks like the real medicine. The blue one I was taking morning and night.
[SEG0023] person_1 (NURSE): Blue is salbutamol, the reliever. The canister he has brought says one hundred micrograms per puff.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Hundred? No. The chemist pack at home is two hundred micrograms. That is the one I use.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, a pop-up came, say the strength again. And how many times are you taking it?
[SEG0026] person_1 (NURSE): I am reading salbutamol one hundred micrograms on this canister. He is saying the home inhaler is two hundred micrograms.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, two hundred. I am taking it maybe five, six times a day when the chest is bad. Today also, same thing.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Five or six times a day of the reliever. That is a lot, even if you feel it is a small matter.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): It is not a lot. Two puffs and it settles in one minute, so where is the problem? It is not too much.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the brown pump, do you know the actual name of it?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't remember the name. Brown cap, I take it when I feel like, not daily. It does not work fast, so I skip it.
[SEG0032] person_1 (NURSE): On the chart the brown inhaler is beclometasone, two hundred micrograms, two puffs twice a day. That one is the preventer.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Two puffs twice? I was doing one puff at night only, and that too maybe four days in a week. I skip it, as I said.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): One second, I was typing the peak flow. How often do you really take the brown one? Say it once more.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): About four days in a week, one puff at night. Sometimes I forget. It is not an important medicine, doctor.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): So, because the screen ate my last line: blue is salbutamol, the reliever, only when you are wheezy. Brown is beclometasone, every day twice a day, even on good days. You have swapped them in your head.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): If you say so. I still feel the brown one helps the tightness faster. Anyway, you are the doctor.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): It will not open the airway in the moment. Let me listen, deep breaths, and stop talking for a second.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): See, I can breathe completely fine. This is all drama.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): There is a wheeze on both sides, scattered wheeze. The chest is not silent. You are speaking in full sentences, which is reassuring.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): So mild only, like I have been saying from the start. Nothing to write a long note about.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergy? Prednisolone, penicillin, anything at all?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergy to anything. Nothing.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Asthma is already on your record, correct? Were you ever admitted, or in ICU?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): They have written asthma, yes, but I don't treat it as a real illness. Admitted? Never. No ICU.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke? Sorry, the cursor jumped, I am asking about smoking.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't smoke. Well, actually I used to, at college. I stopped three years... no, four years back.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stopped four years ago. Anyone in the family with asthma?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): My father has asthma. He is the serious one, not me.
[SEG0050] person_1 (NURSE): I have entered the peak flow as three hundred. He is still saying the blow was three twenty.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will go with your reading, three hundred. Personal best on the old file is five hundred and fifty, so three hundred is low for him.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): That personal best is ancient. I was not even trying properly today, the mouthpiece was loose.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Even so. This looks to me like an asthma flare after that viral cold. Working impression only, not a final label. It is not just the cold hanging on.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): You are making it big. It will go by itself in a few days, these things do.
[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am adding a steroid tablet course. Prednisolone thirty milligrams... no, sorry, forty milligrams, once a day, for five days, with food in the morning.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Tablets for five days, for this small wheeze? Kindly don't frighten my mother with that.
[SEG0057] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. It is to settle the flare. Keep the salbutamol for when you are actually wheezy, not five or six times if we can help it.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, okay. And what do I do with the brown one, then?

[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): Beclometasone two hundred micrograms, two puffs twice a day, every single day. Do not take the brown one for sudden tightness. If you have no spacer, pharmacy will give you one today.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't have a spacer. I will try to remember the twice a day, no promise.
[SEG0061] person_3 (DOCTOR): We might do a chest x-ray if it does not settle, not from here today. I don't want one just for the sake of it.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): X-ray for a cold leftover? No need. I am telling you plainly.
[SEG0063] person_3 (DOCTOR): Only if it does not settle. Let's see you in two weeks, in this clinic.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks is too soon, and the parking here is a headache. If I am fine I will cancel.
[SEG0065] person_3 (DOCTOR): Still book it. If you are worse before that, breathless while resting, or the blue inhaler is not holding you, go to emergency, don't wait for me.
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): It will not come to that. I know my own chest.
[SEG0067] person_1 (NURSE): Shall I book the two-week slot at the desk, doctor? The afternoon clinic usually has space.
[SEG0068] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, book the two-week visit. And print the prednisolone, forty milligrams, for five days.
[SEG0069] person_1 (NURSE): I will. Sir, any other tablet at home, blood pressure or sugar or anything?
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only these two pumps. I am otherwise healthy, I keep saying.
[SEG0071] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, repeat that, the screen jumped back. Any other regular medicine, and the allergy line, just to confirm?
[SEG0072] person_2 (PATIENT): No other medicine. No allergy. I told you already, doctor.
[SEG0073] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. The cough at night, from you yourself, not from your mother. What actually happens?
[SEG0074] person_2 (PATIENT): The cough is a little in the daytime. At night I am okay. I don't wake up coughing.
[SEG0075] person_1 (NURSE): His mother was very firm on this. She said he was awake from two o'clock, coughing and wheezing, and he did not go back to sleep.
[SEG0076] person_2 (PATIENT): She was asleep herself, how will she know. I woke once for water. I was not coughing.
[SEG0077] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the two stories don't match. I will leave the night cough and the sleep as not clear. The daytime wheeze and the little cough, you do accept.
[SEG0078] person_2 (PATIENT): Little bit only. Don't put a big heading on the file.
[SEG0079] person_3 (DOCTOR): About that cold. Any sore throat now, any running nose still?
[SEG0080] person_2 (PATIENT): Running nose was there, it stopped. The throat was scratchy for two days, that also finished. Nothing now.

[SEG0081] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. Prednisolone from today, forty milligrams once a day, five days. Blue inhaler only when wheezy. Brown inhaler every day. Chest x-ray only if you are not better. I will see you in two weeks.
[SEG0082] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine, I will take the tablets. Don't tell amma it is serious, she will not sleep, and then I will not sleep.
[SEG0083] person_1 (NURSE): I will just tell her the plan, not that it is serious. Peak flow stays entered as three hundred, whatever he heard.
[SEG0084] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Collect the tablets and a spacer from pharmacy on the way out. We are done, Arjun, go before this computer crashes again.

spec.situation: Teenager or adult wheezy after a cold; confuses blue and brown inhaler; uses the reliever 'maybe five, six times a day'; peak flow numbers read by the nurse. Doctor adds a steroid course.
features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Charted regimen and preventer role supported, but patient's actual use is one puff nightly about four days/week, not prescribed frequency.
bad.text: beclometasone inhaler (generic_name=beclometasone, dose=200 micrograms, frequency=2 puffs twice a day, indication=asthma preventer, status=currently_used, reported_by=nurse)

omissions.text: Current salbutamol inhaler dose was stated as two puffs each time, used maybe 5–6 times a day when the chest is bad, including today; the brought canister was read as 100 micrograms per puff and the patient said the home inhaler is 200 micrograms per puff.

Beclometasone actual use was recorded wrongly as if he is taking the prescribed regimen; the patient said he actually takes one puff at night only, about four days a week, sometimes forgets, and does not take it daily.
Prednisolone plan included taking it with food in the morning.
No spacer at home was confirmed by the patient.
Doctor noted old-file personal best peak flow of 550 L/min, making the current 300 low for him.
Negative finding: patient denied any current sore throat and any ongoing running nose; both had finished.
Negative finding: patient denied waking at night coughing.
Negative finding: patient denied current smoking (former smoker only).
Past medication history/other meds: patient said he takes no other regular medicines, including no blood pressure or diabetes tablets.
